title: Elasticity: How Sensitive Markets Are to Price and Income

questions.question: Price rises by 10% and quantity demanded falls by 20%. Price elasticity of demand is:
questions.rationale: PED = %ΔQd ÷ %ΔP = 20/10 = 2, which exceeds 1, so demand is elastic.

questions.question: The single most important determinant of price elasticity of demand is:
questions.rationale: The more close substitutes exist, the easier buyers switch away when price rises — the biggest driver of elasticity.

questions.question: A perfectly inelastic demand curve is:
questions.rationale: PED = 0 means quantity demanded does not respond to price at all, so the curve is vertical — e.g., a life-saving medicine.

questions.question: When demand is inelastic, a seller who raises the price will find that total revenue:
questions.rationale: With PED < 1, quantity falls proportionally less than price rises, so revenue P × Q increases — the reason sin taxes target inelastic goods.

questions.question: The midpoint (arc) method of computing elasticity is preferred because it:
options: Removes the sign of the answer
Gives the same value whichever direction the price moves
questions.rationale: The arc method averages both endpoints, so elasticity computed from A to B equals that from B to A.

questions.question: A good with a negative income elasticity of demand is called:
questions.rationale: YED < 0 means demand falls as income rises — the mark of an inferior good such as coarse grains or generic brands.

questions.question: Cross elasticity of demand between petrol and cars is expected to be:
questions.rationale: Complements have XED < 0: costlier petrol reduces driving and hence the demand for cars.

questions.question: For a necessity good with an income elasticity between 0 and 1, as household income rises, the share of income spent on it:
questions.rationale: With YED < 1, spending on the good grows more slowly than income, so its budget share declines — Engel's observation about food.

questions.question: Demand for a product is more elastic in the long run than the short run because:
options: Habits, contracts, and durable stocks adjust only slowly over time
Substitutes disappear in the long run
questions.rationale: Consumers need time to adjust habits and replace durables, so quantity responses grow larger with the time horizon.

questions.question: According to the lesson's illustrative ladder, which category shows the highest price elasticity?
questions.rationale: Air travel — a discretionary luxury with substitutes and a large budget share — sits at the top of the elasticity ladder, around 2.5.
